verdict.label: Full review
verdict.summary: Self-serve to create and test, but the free Starter tier caps you at 5 connected organisations; Core ($35 AUD/mo) allows 50, and anything beyond needs app certification and a security assessment.
verdict.cost: Free for 5 connections; $35 AUD/mo for 50; certification + $245+ AUD/mo beyond

composioFit.summary: Composio does not provide a managed Xero app, so you must bring your own OAuth app and configure the auth config in the Composio dashboard.
whyOwnApp: Control over brand name on OAuth consent screens
Dedicated rate limits and connection capacity per app

phases.name: Create Xero App
steps: Log into the Xero Developer Portal
Create a new OAuth2 app, select the Auth Code or PKCE grant type, and obtain your Client ID and Client Secret
phases.handoff: Copy your Client ID and Client Secret into the Composio dashboard auth config.

phases.name: Configure Redirect URI and Scopes
steps: Add the Composio callback redirect URI into your Xero app settings
Select the required granular scopes for your integration
phases.handoff: Proceed to test authentication with your own account.

phases.name: Test Connection
steps: Initiate the OAuth flow via Composio using your Xero credentials
Verify token exchange and tenant connections retrieval
phases.handoff: App is ready for beta testing with up to 5 starter connections.

artefacts.title: Xero App Registration Details
artefacts.body:
App Name: Your AI Agent Integration

artefacts.title: Scope Justification for Xero API
artefacts.body: We request openid profile email for single sign-on identification, accounting.transactions for viewing and managing business transactions, and offline_access to maintain persistent background access for our AI agent via refresh tokens.

requirements.when: Until you move to a paid tier

scopes.purpose: Obtain refresh tokens to maintain offline connection
View and manage Feed Connections 2.0 and Statements 1.0

redirectRules.rule: Must be an https address, although http://localhost/ can be used for testing. http://127.0.0.1 cannot be used.

blockers.symptom: The 6th customer can't connect their Xero organisation
blockers.fix: Upgrade the app to Core (up to 50 connections) in the Xero developer portal.
blockers.fallback: Disconnect unused/test tenants to free connections while you upgrade.

blockers.symptom: <message> You have reached the limit of invoices you can approve. </message>
blockers.cause: Xero organisations using the Early pricing plan exceeded their monthly invoice creation limit via API.
blockers.fix: Upgrade the Xero organisation pricing plan or reduce invoice creation volume.
blockers.fallback: Handle HTTP 400 response code in client logic and notify the user.

blockers.cause: Exceeded concurrency, minute, or daily API rate limits.
blockers.fix: Pause requests and respect the Retry-After HTTP header and X-Rate-Limit-Problem headers.
blockers.fallback: Batch requests up to 50 nodes per request and use Rapid Sync if applicable.

blockers.symptom: Refresh token expired or invalid after grace period
blockers.cause: Refresh tokens expire after 60 days, and retry grace periods expire after 30 minutes if rotation fails.
blockers.fix: Prompt the user to re-authorise the API application to generate a new refresh token.
blockers.fallback: Re-trigger the standard OAuth authorization code flow via Composio.

checklist.text: Register an OAuth2 app in the Xero Developer Portal
Copy Client ID and Client Secret into the Composio Auth Config
Configure the Composio callback redirect URI in Xero
Request minimum necessary granular scopes and offline_access
Test OAuth connection and token exchange with your own account

claims.text: Xero’s API supports the authorization code grant type using standard authorization code flow or PKCE, and custom connections using client credentials.
claims.quote: Xero’s API supports the authorization code grant type using the standard authorization code flow or the Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE) extension. We also have a premium integration option called C

claims.text: New apps default to the starter tier with a limit of 5 connections.
claims.quote: New apps default to the starter tier with 5 connections.

claims.text: Xero offers plans including Starter, Core, Plus, Advanced, and Enterprise based on connections and data egress volume.
claims.quote: introducing five plans: Starter, Core, Plus, Advanced, Enterprise.

claims.text: Composio does not have a managed OAuth app for Xero, so you must bring your own OAuth app.
claims.quote: Composio-managed OAuth available? No

claims.text: You can create a custom auth config in the Composio dashboard by providing your Client ID and Client Secret.
claims.quote: For OAuth toolkits, register an app in the provider's developer portal and add the redirect URI from the dashboard. Then copy the Client ID and Client Secret back into Composio.

claims.text: To get started, create an OAuth2 app and make sure you select the Auth Code grant type to receive a Client ID and Client Secret.
claims.quote: To get started, create an OAuth2 app and make sure you select the “Auth Code” grant type. Your app is assigned a unique Client ID and you can then generate a Client Secret.

claims.text: The redirect URI must be an https address, though http://localhost/ can be used for testing.
claims.quote: redirect_uri the URL on your server to redirect back to – This must be an https address, however for testing you can use http://localhost/ Please note that http://127.0.0.1 cannot be used

claims.text: The redirect URI must be HTTPS, or http://localhost/ for testing, while http://127.0.0.1 cannot be used.
claims.quote: redirect_uri the URL on your server to redirect back to – This must be an https address, however for testing you can use http://localhost/ Please note that http://127.0.0.1 cannot be used

claims.text: All new and existing Web and PKCE apps have been assigned granular scopes such as accounting.transactions.
claims.quote: Web and PKCE apps – Since March 2026, all new and existing Web and PKCE apps have been assigned granular scopes.

claims.text: Authorization codes expire 5 minutes after issuance and can be exchanged for an access token via a POST request to the token endpoint.
claims.quote: code a temporary code that may only be exchanged once and expires 5 minutes after issuance.

claims.text: Use OpenID scopes to retrieve details about the user’s identity, which are required for single sign on.
claims.quote: Use OpenID scopes to retrieve details about the user’s identity. These are required for single sign on.

claims.text: To get a refresh token, you must request the offline_access scope.
claims.quote: To get a refresh token, you must request the offline_access scope.

claims.text: New partner integrations should request bankfeedsv2 for Feed Connections 2.0 and Statements 1.0.
claims.quote: New partner integrations should request bankfeedsv2 for Feed Connections 2.0 and Statements 1.0.

claims.text: To access the Practice Manager API you need to register as an app partner and complete a security self-assessment questionnaire.
claims.quote: To access the Practice Manager API you will need to first register as an app partner and complete a security self-assessment questionnaire.

claims.text: The Journals endpoint is a premium feature requiring security assessment and use case approval.
claims.quote: Keep in mind the Journals endpoint is a premium feature for apps in the Advanced tier and above.

claims.text: Exceeding the invoice limit returns an HTTP 400 response with message You have reached the limit of invoices you can approve.
claims.quote: < message > You have reached the limit of invoices you can approve. </ message >

claims.text: Exceeding a rate limit results in an HTTP 429 response containing an X-Rate-Limit-Problem header and a Retry-After header.
claims.quote: Exceeding a rate limit will result in an HTTP 429 (too many requests) response. It will include an X-Rate-Limit-Problem header telling you which limit you have reached.

claims.text: Access tokens expire after 30 minutes, refresh tokens expire after 60 days, and there is a 30 minute grace period to retry using an existing refresh token.
claims.quote: Access tokens expire after 30 minutes. Your app can refresh an access token without user interaction by using a refresh token... Refresh tokens expire after 60 days.

claims.text: New Xero apps default to the Starter tier with 5 connections.
claims.quote: New apps default to the starter tier with 5 connections.

claims.text: Moving to the Core tier allows up to 50 connections.
claims.quote: Moving up to Core will give you up to 50 connections.

claims.text: Listing on the Xero App Store requires the Plus tier or above.
claims.quote: To be listed on the App Store, you will need to be in the Plus tier or above.

claims.text: Monthly tier fees: Starter no charge, Core $35 AUD, Plus $245 AUD, Advanced $1445 AUD, Enterprise price on application.
claims.quote: Monthly Tier Fee No charge $35 AUD $245 AUD $1445 AUD Price on Application

claims.text: Maximum connections per tier: 5 / 50 / 1000 / 10,000 / no limit.
claims.quote: Connections (maximum) 5 50 1000 10,000

claims.text: Certification matters beyond tiers: each Xero organisation can connect at most five uncertified apps, while certified apps have no such limit.
claims.quote: each organisation or practice is limited to connecting a maximum of five uncertified apps. There is no limit on connecting certified apps.

uncertainties: Exact turnaround time for Xero App Store review and certification is not explicitly quantified in days.
Detailed requirements for submitting an app to the Plus Tier App Store review queue beyond having 10 beta customers are not fully documented in the text.
